name: Tsez
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Alekseev & Radzhabov 2004 'Tsez' (grammar sketch); Comrie & Polinsky 2020 'Tsez'; Polinsky 2015 Tsez Syntax (lingbuzz/002315, read: syntax only, no stress statement)

new_statements.quote: [с. 329] Акцентная система изучена недостаточно, поэтому тон не транскрибируется в словаре. По предварительным данным, в цезском представлена система со слоговым тоном, типичная для андо-цезского ареала. Словесное ударение отсутствует. [с. 9] В словаре не приводятся акцентологические характеристики следующих говоров: ТИНД, ЦЕЗ, ГИН, БЕЖХ, ГУНЗ, ЛАК, ЦАХГ, ЦАХЦ, КРЫЗ, БУД, УД. Словесное ударение в этих говорах отсутствует. [с. 318] В языках со слоговым тоном обычно отсутствует словесное ударение ... Если на слово падает фразовый акцент, то он помещается либо на первый слог слова, либо на "тяжелый" непервый (то есть закрытый слог или слог с долгим гласным).
new_statements.translation: [p. 329] The accentual system is insufficiently studied, therefore tone is not transcribed in the word list. According to preliminary data, Tsez has a system with syllabic tone, typical of the Andic-Tsezic area. Word stress is absent. [p. 9] The dictionary gives no accentological characteristics for the following varieties: Tindi, TSEZ, Hinuq, Bezhta (Kh.), Hunzib, Lak, Tsakhur (G, Ts), Kryz, Budukh, Udi. Word stress is absent in these varieties. [p. 318] In languages with syllabic tone word stress is usually absent ... If a phrasal accent falls on a word, it is placed either on the first syllable of the word or on a 'heavy' non-first syllable (i.e. a closed syllable or one with a long vowel).
new_statements.citation: Кибрик А.Е., Кодзасов С.В. 1990. Сопоставительное изучение дагестанских языков. Имя. Фонетика. Москва: Изд-во Московского университета. Part III «Фонетика» (phonetic sketches by S.V. Kodzasov from MSU field expeditions), §7 «Цезский язык (с. Кидеро)», «Слог и просодия», пункт 3.
new_statements.locator: p. 329 (Tsez sketch pp. 328-329; PDF page 329); supporting statements p. 9 (Part I intro) and p. 318 (general Daghestanian prosody)
new_statements.reading: no word stress according to the source
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kodzasov's first-hand field sketch of the Kidero variety states that Tsez has no word stress; its accentual system is, on preliminary evidence, one of syllabic (lexical) tone like the rest of the Andic-Tsezic area, but was too little studied to be transcribed. Prominence heard on words is treated as phrasal accent, which in such Daghestanian systems goes to the first syllable or to a heavy (closed / long-vowel) non-initial syllable.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned by Kibrik & Kodzasov. (The secondary ILing RAN 'Малые языки России' page instead claims weak, dynamic, non-fixed stress with main stress on the initial syllable and a secondary stress on the final or penultimate syllable in words of three or more syllables — unsourced, probably after Imnaishvili 1963.)
new_statements.exceptions: None in the source; the authors flag the whole accentual analysis as preliminary ('изучена недостаточно', 'по предварительным данным'). Conflicting descriptions exist: ILing minlang page (weak dynamic initial stress, not fixed); Comrie & Polinsky 2017/2020 only say prosodic contrasts have been noted (citing this very page and NCED p.115) and remain uninvestigated; Maddieson et al. 1996 explicitly defer stress and intonation to future work.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level claim based on elicited isolated nominal word forms (comparative noun dictionary) from Kidero village speakers; phrasal accent placement discussed only generically for Daghestanian (p. 318). Variety: Kidero dialect; Comrie & Polinsky's material is Asakh (Tsebari).
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement (Kibrik & Kodzasov 1990) describes the speech of the village of Kidero (ЦЕЗ = «цезский, с. Кидеро»), i.e. the Kidero dialect of Tsez proper; Comrie & Polinsky's sketch follows the Tsebari subdialect of Asakh; Maddieson et al. 1996 recorded one speaker (R. Rajabov). All are Tsez proper (dido1241), not the divergent Sagada dialect. No separate glottocode asserted for Kidero.

sources.note: p.329: accent system insufficiently studied, tone not transcribed; by preliminary data Tsez has a syllabic-tone system typical of the Andic-Tsezic area; 'Словесное ударение отсутствует' (word stress is absent). p.9: ЦЕЗ listed among varieties with no accentological marking, 'word stress is absent in these varieties'. p.318 (general): all Andic and Tsezic languages have syllabic tonal accent; in such languages word stress is usually absent; phrasal accent, if on a word, goes to the first syllable or a heavy non-first syllable.

sources.note: Neither article has any statement on stress/accent.

sources.citation: «Цезский язык». Малые языки России, проект Института языкознания РАН (minlang.iling-ran.ru), web page ©2019-2026, section «Фонетика» (no author or source given for the passage).
sources.note: Verbatim: 'Ударение в цезском языке большей частью слабое, динамическое. Вместе с тем, оно не фиксировано. Указывают на существование второстепенного ударения, которое имеется в трехсложных и состоящих из большего количества слогов словах. Отметим также, что основное ударение падает на начальный слог, а второстепенное ударение - на первый или второй слог с конца.' Secondary/unsourced (bibliography lists Imnaishvili 1963 and Bokarev 1959); contradicts Kibrik & Kodzasov.
